question.problem:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-{e}^{-x})(1-{e}^{-y}), & x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0.$

Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1, \; y \geq 0.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x, y)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y) = \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x \partial y} F(x,y).
$$

For $0 \leq x \leq 1$ and $y \geq 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}(1-{e}^{-y}))) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\frac{∂}{∂y}(1-{e}^{-y})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{e}^{-y}) \\  & ={e}^{-y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}) \\  & ={e}^{-y}\cdot 2x \\  & =2x{e}^{-y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Otherwise, $f(x,y) = 0.$

Therefore, we have
